heading: ## The leg ledger — replay, receipt, and how it is read (round 7, measured)

findings.quote: the ten-leg registry itself enumerates and executes without skips] (round 52: the ten legs report no skipped case on this host
findings.why: At C0 the bracket's two halves answer the same question oppositely, and the host-scoped half is falsified by the ledger's own execution on this host. Receipt 04: leg 2's target at its pinned bytes (sha256 275d8294… = PIN_BASH) prints `skip-case 15 verbs-sandboxed` / `skip-case 16 verbs-break-injection` … `substrate-absent (handler not on PATH)` and `SELFTEST: PASS (16 cases)` with 14 ok-case lines, and a real `--regression` leg at C0's bytes carries 22 such lines in its sweep.log. The ledger's own row 2 states the same: '16 cases (14 hermetic + 2 substrate-gated `skip-case`)' (receipt 06). So 'the ten legs report no skipped case on this host' is true only if 'report' means the runner receipt (which has no skip field at :78-79); the sentence's own opener ('enumerated, executed and skipped counts distinguished') and round 53's own finding put the subject at case level. The closing clause 'the ten-leg registry itself … executes without skips' then re-asserts, under an undefined subject ('registry'), the exact absolute T53W2R6 F1 refuted and that the same bracket calls 'overstated' six words earlier. Net: the correction closes the quoted defect lexically only — the round-52 parenthetical F1 asked to scope or drop was kept, and the refuted claim reappears in a new subject, so a reader cannot tell which reading the page intends.

findings.quote: `REGRESSION_CASE js-kimi-census: FAIL (out of band: killed-delta=1 flips=1)`
findings.why: The tool never emits that line with its parenthesis closed there: `tools/mutate-and-run.sh:1400` formats `'REGRESSION_CASE %s: FAIL (out of band:%s; log: %s)'`, and a FAIL measured at C0's bytes reads `REGRESSION_CASE bash-surface-census: FAIL (out of band: killed-delta=1 flips=1; log: /…/sweep.log)` (receipt 04:C). Step 3's own rule is 'Quote the rows, never the word', and a reader copying the quoted string into grep gets no match; the lane's own audit quoted the same line with the ellipsis the page omits (`FAIL (out of band: killed-delta=1 flips=1…)`, reports/r7-aud-t7.md §3 F4). Severity is low: the mechanism and the arithmetic all reproduce (receipt 04:C: REGRESSION_DEFECT → match=9/10 flips=1 → FAIL), so this is quoted-line shape (grep exactness), not a false claim about how FAIL names its rows.

findings.quote: Measured instance (T7-1, 2026-10-14; replayed by this lane under the same tool sha `cf41efaa…`)
findings.why: 'T7-1' is a lane id in this page's vocabulary (T7-2, T8-2, T52W2Fix06 are lanes) while the revision is written `r7-1` six times in the same section; the two readings have opposite truth values and the sentence names no receipt for the instance. Lane reading is false by the lane's own records: T7-1/T7-2's round-7 measurement was `REGRESSION: PASS (cases=2 passed=2; band killed-delta<=1 flips<=1)` on the r6 harness `b56c6e57` (receipt 06: ledger §5, lines 162-166), and the four-leg exact-band instance is T8-2's run at 2026-10-14T19:14:16Z (`corpus/knowledge/mutation-case-kumitate-claims.md` §6), corroborated by AUD-T7's 18:34:47Z primary run (`reports/r7-aud-t7.md` §1) — neither is T7-1. Revision reading ('r7-1') holds exactly (receipt 06: four legs, every `match=10/10 … flips=0`, `REGRESSION: PASS (cases=4 passed=4; ledger legs exact: killed-delta<=0 flips<=0)`, rc 0). No number is wrong; the defect is that one token carries two referents with opposite truth values and the item cites no artifact for the instance it asserts.
